items.title: The Week That Was, The Week Ahead: Macro and Markets
items.take: The damage bill from week 47: Nvidia fell 22.9% across five sessions and is down nearly 50% from its October 6 peak, and the Nasdaq is now negative for 2026 while the S&P 500 and Dow barely hold positive returns. The week ahead is holiday-shortened, with Workday and Deere earnings and Friday's October PCE inflation read the main markers.

items.title: The S&P 500 fell into a correction as an SEC report sank Nvidia
items.take: The weekend's calendar of what comes next: markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and at 1 p.m. Friday, Jensen Huang sits for closed-door interviews with three House committees on December 1, and the Fed meets December 8-9. Adobe expects $12.9 billion of online Black Friday spending, up 9.2%. Its verdict on Nvidia: a trust story now, record sales lost to an SEC report and an empty chair.

items.title: Micron plunges 13% as Barron's calls memory stocks 'agonizingly cheap'
items.take: The contrarian weekend read: even after Friday's 13% plunge, Barron's argues the memory-chip names are agonizingly cheap, with Micron at roughly 3.4 times the earnings analysts expect for its fiscal year versus 15 to 20 times for the typical S&P 500 stock, and the average analyst target implying almost 150% upside. Even after the drop Micron is still up 111% this year.

items.title: What held up in the rout: defensives and healthcare as money rotated out of tech
items.take: Not everything fell: UnitedHealth rose 2.84%, AT&T gained 2.11%, and consumer staples like Colgate-Palmolive and Kraft Heinz each climbed 1.89% as money rotated out of high-growth technology. The piece's watch list for the short week centers on Nvidia, Workday, Deere and the Thanksgiving-week PCE data.

items.title: Not a flight to cash: where the money hid in an 8.6% down week
items.take: Friday's breadth was as bad as it gets: only about 1% of the stocks in the broad-market group rose, the second straight day near that level, on roughly $420 billion of institutional volume, the heaviest day in a 30-day window that averages about $267 billion. The takeaway from the flows: this read as rotation within equities, not a stampede into cash.
